taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains the occurrence as unclassified. VIGIL-FC-000048 Verification-Dependency Access Failure was tested because the affected route depended on Microsoft personal-account sign-in, but the preserved evidence does not establish that an otherwise valid or unresolved OpenAI entitlement was blocked solely by verification non-completion or that no proportionate alternative sign-in, grace, cached, or degraded-access route remained available. VIGIL-FC-000032 Access-State Collapse is not established because the provider status record itself distinguishes the affected Microsoft personal-account route from general service availability rather than collapsing multiple access causes into one misleading state. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is also not established because no expiry, revocation, refresh, recovery, replacement, or reauthentication propagation defect is evidenced.

Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000048: the record does not establish an otherwise valid or unresolved entitlement plus absence of proportionate fallback; VIGIL-FC-000032: the affected Microsoft identity route is specifically distinguished rather than collapsed into a generic state; VIGIL-FC-000031: no authentication-state transition propagation defect is evidenced. Primary classification changed: no — remains unclassified. Existing classifications retained: none. External-assessment material was checked where present; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5; the occurrence establishes a third-party identity-route outage without the additional conditions required by the current access-state classes.
